title: Growing people
sub: Film 4 of Ownership and performance, the last of Leading data people: how people grow at work. Goals they help set, feedback every week about the work and its effect, never about who they are, and a next step with more to own.
howto: The film is drawn in ink line: flat colour with one even dark line, and whole people in the places where they work and meet: a village classroom in Japan in the 1870s, classrooms of today in Japan and the United States, and the university's rooms. Its ideas are written by hand: at a board, where a head teacher explains lesson study and a consultant what research says about feedback, and in notebooks, where Ivy, and once Helena, keep what to remember. Its colours mean the same in every film: blue is plans and rules (Ivy's goals), orange is data (Teaching space use), green is something done or of value (each goal met, feedback that helps), and amber a risk or a cost (feedback that turns from the work to the person). People and their clothes wear none of them.
